The shortest frame is a CAN FD base-format frame (11-bit identifier; DroneCAN uses 29-bit identifiers only but shares a bus with CAN 2.0A protocols) with no data and bit-rate switching: SOF, 11 identifier bits, RRS, IDE, FDF and res are 16 bits at 1000 kbit/s; BRS, ESI, 4 DLC bits, the 4-bit stuff count (3 bits and parity), the 17-bit CRC, 6 fixed stuff bits and the CRC delimiter are 34 bits counted at 5000 kbit/s; ACK slot, ACK delimiter, 7 EOF and 3 intermission bits are 12 bits at 1000 kbit/s. 28 us + 6.8 us = 34.8 us is a lower bound: the rate switches at the sample points of BRS and the CRC delimiter, and dynamic stuff bits are left out. 400,000/34.8 = 11,494.3 and 3,000/34.8 = 86.2, each plus one for a frame ending inside the window. Derived from the field layout; ISO 11898-1 was not read. For comparison, a 29-bit FD frame (19 nominal bits more) is at least 53.8 us: 7,435 and 56; a classic 0-byte base frame is 47 us: 8,511 and 64.
